devices_apis: Phone browser (Red-Flag Navigator tapping test)
ResearchKit two-finger tapping task (iOS, open source)
WatchALS custom iPhone app (research)
access: None; runs in the browser today. ResearchKit is open source and needs no special entitlement.
sampling: Active, weekly, about 1 minute per hand; average 2 to 3 trials per session.

mdc.text: About 18 taps per 10 s, or about 35% of the person's baseline, provisional. Scaled from the WatchALS weekly home MDC95 of 35.5 (dominant) and 32.6 (non-dominant) for a 20-s alternating two-finger test; that column is headed %MDC95, so its units may be taps or percent.
mdc.population: 19 people with ALS, weekly home iPhone tests over 24 weeks (WatchALS); scaling to a 10-s single-finger test computed by us

als_evidence: In WatchALS (19 diagnosed ALS, 23 controls, iPhone) people with ALS made fewer taps and taps correlated 0.71 to 0.74 with fine-motor scores, but practice gains hid any decline over 24 weeks. In nQiALS (63 diagnosed ALS, 30 controls) a 30-s phone tapping test separated ALS from controls only modestly (AUC 0.67, 49 against 22 analysed) and not in mild hand involvement (AUC 0.52).
feeds_tool: HOME_TESTS tap_right and tap_left (region arm): weekly mean of same-day trials, MDC 18 taps per 10 s (provisional), baseline after 2 practice weeks; a decline adds home_decline in arm.
pitfalls: Practice gains raise scores for weeks and hide decline; carpal tunnel syndrome also slows tapping; hands differed by about 8 taps in 7 pilot volunteers; phone model, fatigue and time of day add noise; restart the baseline after hand surgery or a splint. The 6-tap placeholder gives about 21% to 33% false alarms per hand over 8 weeks under the engine rule (computed by us).

devices_apis: WatchALS grooved pegboard task (iPhone, research)
ResearchKit hole peg test (iOS, open source)
access: Not built; ResearchKit is open source.
sampling: Active, weekly, each hand.

mdc.text: MDC 12.9 in ALS for both hands (14.5 and 14 in controls), units not stated and the column is headed %MDC95; ICC 0.73 to 0.81 in ALS.
mdc.population: 19 people with ALS, weekly home iPhone tests over 24 weeks (WatchALS)

als_evidence: In WatchALS (19 diagnosed ALS) the digital pegboard correlated 0.71 with fine-motor scores in the dominant hand. It was the only fine-motor task that declined by the end of 24 weeks, in the non-dominant hand.
feeds_tool: Not fed now; a possible second arm test (weekly mean, HOME_TESTS-style) once its units and weekly noise are confirmed.
pitfalls: One small study; lower ICC than tapping; MDC units unclear; dexterity tasks show large practice effects.

devices_apis: In-app copy-typing task
nQ keyboard (nQ Medical, now Area2 AI) on iOS or Android
Neurokeys keyboard (MS research)
Apple SensorKit SRKeyboardMetrics (research-only)
access: A copy task needs no approval; passive logging needs a custom keyboard or Apple's SensorKit research entitlement with ethics approval.
sampling: Active 5-minute copy task, weekly (as in nQiALS); passive logging whenever the person types if a custom keyboard is installed.

mdc.text: No ALS MDC. In MS, 14-day keystroke aggregates had test-retest ICC 0.601 to 0.965 and SEM 0.098 to 0.241 in z-score units (Neurokeys).
mdc.population: 85 people with MS analysed (Lam 2021)

als_evidence: In nQiALS (63 diagnosed ALS, 30 controls) a copy-typing model separated ALS from controls with AUC 0.89 (49 against 22 analysed), and 0.93 in mild hand involvement where tapping scored 0.52, but the passive progression model was weak. Key hold time grew with progression in 19 people typing with a finger accelerometer (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Not fed now; a future arm test (mean flight time from a copy task, lower is better) once weekly noise is measured. Store timing only, never text.
pitfalls: One centre, no external validation, and several industry-affiliated authors; phone model, screen size and autocorrect matter; typing slows with age, and its age signal varies by time of day; privacy risk if text were stored.

devices_apis: Research wrist accelerometers (ActiGraph) in all ALS studies
Apple Watch raw accelerometer through a custom watch app
Wear OS SensorManager (Pixel Watch, Galaxy Watch)
Samsung Health Sensor SDK (25 Hz accelerometer)
Garmin Connect IQ
access: A custom watch app is needed; no aggregated API offers it. Samsung needs a partnership to distribute, and an Apple Watch app needs a Mac.
sampling: Recommended as a 45-second arm-raise task 3 times a week; passive all-day wear (21-hour valid days) also works but adherence is poor.

mdc.text: No MDC published. Test-retest ICC 0.80 to 0.96 for arm-raise metrics across week 1, and 0.84 to 0.90 for a wrist composite score (Gupta 2023).
mdc.population: 257 to 259 of 329 people with ALS who did all three week-1 sessions, ALS TDI ARC study (Straczkiewicz 2026)

als_evidence: Forearm movement counts fell 2.56% to 2.74% a month in 202 diagnosed people (4.4% to 4.9% in a 20-person pilot, computed by us), faster in relative terms than the ALSFRS-R fine-motor score. A 45-second arm-raise task was linked to fine-motor scores (model R squared 0.88 to 0.90) in 329 people, all with research ActiGraph watches.
feeds_tool: Not fed now; a future arm test (weekly median arm-raise intensity, region arm) once a consumer watch port and its weekly noise are checked.
pitfalls: All-day wear is hard to keep up (51.3 of 282.8 days valid); people shift use to the unaffected arm, so read each arm separately; caregivers may help; consumer watches are unvalidated for these metrics; about 5% to 10% change in 8 weeks with no MDC (computed by us).

devices_apis: Home handheld dynamometer (phones have no force sensor)
access: Buy a dynamometer; no platform API checked stores grip.
sampling: Active; daily for 3 months, then twice weekly, in the home study.
als_evidence: In 61 diagnosed people measuring at home, daily grip readings cut the estimated trial size for the right hand from 383 to 101 per arm compared with monthly readings; for the left hand the cut was small (136 to 114). In UK Biobank, grip below 21 kg went with higher later ALS risk, a population finding (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Not fed; the app has no dynamometer input.
pitfalls: Many unexplained missing values; needs a device; units of the published slopes not stated; no MDC.

devices_apis: Any phone as a stopwatch over a measured course (to build in Red-Flag Navigator)
ResearchKit timed walk task (iOS)
WatchALS 60-second walk (iPhone, research)
access: None; a stopwatch version needs no motion sensor and can be built tonight.
sampling: Active, weekly, 2 to 3 walks of about 10 m at usual pace.

mdc.text: MDC95 0.179 m/s in ALS and 0.284 m/s in controls for a weekly home 60-second walk (WatchALS); the table header says %MDC95, so treat as approximate. Recommend 0.28 m/s before diagnosis and 0.18 m/s after.
mdc.population: 19 people with ALS and 23 controls, weekly home tests over 24 weeks (WatchALS)

als_evidence: In WatchALS (19 diagnosed ALS) gait speed had ICC 0.93 and correlated 0.83 with gross-motor scores, and in a home shoe-sensor study (9 diagnosed ALS) speed fell 0.021 m/s a month, or 0.135 m/s a month before a switch to a walking aid. Clinic 6-minute walks in 186 ambulatory people with ALS reached 66% of predicted (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Replace HOME_TESTS walk: unit m/s, higherIsBetter true, region leg, weekly mean of 2 to 3 timed walks, MDC 0.28 m/s before diagnosis and 0.18 m/s after; a decline adds home_decline in leg.
pitfalls: An average decliner needs about 8.6 months to pass the MDC and a fast decliner about 1.3 months (computed by us); walking aids and ankle braces change speed, so restart the baseline; home speed runs slower than clinic speed; repeat walks gain a few metres.

devices_apis: Phone motion sensor in the browser (current walk mockup)
Foot or ankle sensors (research)
access: Browser motion permission over HTTPS; see the AirPods report for the build.
sampling: Active walk of 60 to 90 seconds (about 50 clean strides) with the phone at the waist.

mdc.text: No ALS MDC. Test-retest ICC under 0.20 for the stride-time coefficient of variation in most conditions (mean stride time 0.96).
mdc.population: 69 healthy older adults and 14 people with frontotemporal dementia, immediate retest (Beauchet 2011, abstract only)

als_evidence: Ambulatory people with diagnosed ALS (42) had higher stance- and swing-time variability than 16 controls on a wearable gait device, and our analysis of public foot-sensor data showed a median 4.86% against 2.53% in controls, in groups not age-matched (computed by us). In 182 people with an ankle sensor, stride-duration variability correlated -0.42 with gross-motor scores and changed less than steps (preprint).
feeds_tool: Current HOME_TESTS walk entry (placeholder MDC 1.0, no published basis): stop feeding it and report it only as an exploratory output with at least about 50 strides.
pitfalls: The least reliable gait measure; phone variability estimates have poor validity; 10 strides bias estimates 26% low (computed by us); needs a fixed phone position and no change of walking aid.

devices_apis: iPhone 8 or later: HealthKit walkingSpeed
Apple Health export (XML)
access: HealthKit read permission in a native app, or the Health app's Export All Health Data with no app; iPhone only.
sampling: Passive, 10 to 30 samples on a typical day while the phone is carried near the waist; none in wheelchair mode; reduce to a weekly median.

mdc.text: MDC95 0.20 m/s (seniors) and 0.22 m/s (adults) for one supervised 6-minute walk, retested after 1 week; Apple's within-visit MDC 0.08 to 0.23 m/s; no published weekly noise.
mdc.population: 24 healthy seniors with usable retests (28 tested, mean age 75.6), iPhone SE in a trouser pocket (Sci Rep 2023)

als_evidence: No ALS study has used HealthKit walking speed; gait speed itself falls in ALS when measured in timed walks. Closest evidence outside ALS: after lower-limb fracture, iPhone walking speed fell 0.200 m/s from injury to 8 weeks (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Context only for now; later perhaps a leg test on the weekly median with a person-specific MDC estimated from the weeks before the visit.
pitfalls: Needs the phone in a pocket near the hip and height set; 21.1% of retests had no gait data, possibly from loose trousers; walking aids reduce accuracy; iPhone only (about 65% of Canadian and 52% of US mobile web use); history may be cut by the iOS 27 recent-window option.

devices_apis: iPhone 8 or later: HealthKit walkingStepLength, walkingDoubleSupportPercentage, walkingAsymmetryPercentage
HealthKit appleWalkingSteadiness (iOS 15 or later, read-only)
access: HealthKit read permission or the Health export; Walking Steadiness is read-only.
sampling: Passive, 10 to 30 samples a day for step metrics; Walking Steadiness weekly, with an alert about a month after a drop into Low.

mdc.text: Step length MDC95 6.1 cm (seniors) to 9.4 cm (adults); double support 1.8% to 3.4%; no MDC for asymmetry or Walking Steadiness.
mdc.population: 24 healthy seniors with usable retests (28 tested), 1-week retest during a supervised 6-minute walk (Sci Rep 2023)

als_evidence: No ALS study has used these metrics, and we found no published validation of Walking Steadiness. Indirectly, gait variability is higher in ALS on research gait sensors.
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: Double support ICC 0.53 in Apple's validation; asymmetry was induced with a knee brace for testing, which Apple says may differ from neurodegenerative disease; Walking Steadiness lags by weeks.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 3 or later: HealthKit sixMinuteWalkTestDistance
access: HealthKit read permission; recalibration after an injury needs an Apple entitlement.
sampling: Passive weekly estimate from the previous 4 weeks; needs at least 3 days with over 8 hours of wear in the past week and 10 such days in 4 weeks.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 47 m for the median person (97 m at the 90th percentile), computed by us from week-to-week SDs of 17 m and 35 m in Apple's validation.
mdc.population: Adults 65 and older in Apple's validation set (Santa Clara Valley)

als_evidence: No ALS study has used the watch estimate. The clinic test it imitates is reduced in ALS: 186 ambulatory people with ALS reached 66% of predicted, correlating 0.71 with gross-motor scores (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: The 4-week window and calibration lag blur fast change; noisier in walker users; validated only in older adults in one region; Apple Watch and iPhone only.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 5 or later: HealthKit stairAscentSpeed and stairDescentSpeed
HealthKit flightsClimbed (iPhone, Apple Watch)
Health Connect FloorsClimbedRecord
Google Health API floors
access: Per-type read permission.
sampling: Passive, about 20 samples on a typical day when stairs are used.
als_evidence: No ALS study measured stair speed or flights climbed. Indirectly, accelerometry during short limb exercises in 350 diagnosed people (tested on 83 held out) predicted the ALSFRS-R stair-climbing item with AUC 0.701.
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: No published accuracy data; depends on whether the person uses stairs at all; none in wheelchair mode.

devices_apis: Apple Watch SE, Series 4 or later, Ultra: Fall Detection and HealthKit numberOfTimesFallen
Core Motion CMFallDetectionManager (real-time, entitlement)
access: HealthKit read permission; real-time events need an Apple entitlement. Fall Detection turns on automatically from age 55; from 18 to 55 a new watch turns it on only during workouts.
sampling: Event-driven; records only falls the wearer confirms or that escalate to emergency services.
als_evidence: Falls are common early in diagnosed ALS: 47% of walkers fell within 3 months and 59% reported falls at the 6-month follow-up (66 people, abstract only), and 11.3% of UK Biobank cases had a recorded fall in the 5 years before diagnosis. No study has tested watch fall detection in ALS.
feeds_tool: Not a home test: a recorded fall prompts the clinician to ask and record falls in a note (Mei weight 2.70, region leg, not a motor sign). Also ask weekly about falls and near-falls.
pitfalls: Detection misses about 18% to 43% of real falls (computed by us); dismissed alerts are not recorded; an Apple Watch caught only 14 of 300 wheelchair falls; under 55 it is on by default only during workouts.

devices_apis: HealthKit stepCount (iPhone, Apple Watch)
Health Connect StepsRecord (Android 14 phone itself and most brands)
Google Health API steps (Fitbit, Pixel Watch)
Garmin Health API dailies and epochs
Withings getintradayactivity
access: Per-type read permission; Google Health API restricted scopes (100 users unverified); Garmin Personal key; Withings free plan.
sampling: Passive, continuous while carried or worn; reduce to a weekly median, preferring peak measures.

mdc.text: MDC 1580 steps a day (27% of the mean), ICC 0.89, Garmin Vivosmart 4 over 5 days.
mdc.population: 104 people with Parkinson's disease (Bianchini 2025, abstract only)

als_evidence: Several diagnosed ALS cohorts show steady declines: a consumer Fitbit Sense counted about 14% fewer steps than a research wrist sensor (34 people) and showed a similar decline (18 people with 6 months or more of data), and phone step counts fell about 8.6% a month (45 people, computed by us). Peak 6-minute wrist activity needed fewer trial participants than the ALSFRS-R for trials longer than 12 months (95 people).
feeds_tool: Context only, region general; never a motor-region decline.
pitfalls: Season (394.5 more steps a day in summer than winter), holidays, phone carrying (iPhone steps 21.5% off in daily life), walking aids (wrist error near 100% with a rollator), firmware updates (Oura minus 20%, Pixel Watch doubled), wear decay. Low activity before diagnosis is a population risk marker, not an individual sign.

devices_apis: Phone GPS in a research app (for example Beiwe)
access: Location permission in a custom app; no consumer health platform stores it as a metric.
sampling: Passive, duty-cycled (Beiwe: 1 minute on, 10 minutes off).
als_evidence: In 45 diagnosed people over about 10 months, home time and distance travelled did not change significantly, although both were associated with self-entered ALSFRS-R scores across visits. During COVID-19 restrictions, home time rose from 19.4 to 23.7 hours a day in 8 people (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: Lockdowns, weather and life changes dominate; Android phones had more GPS gaps than iPhones; location is sensitive data; battery drain.

devices_apis: Withings scales (Getmeas measure type 1, webhook category 1)
Fitbit Aria scales (Google Health API weight)
Garmin Index scale (Garmin Health API)
HealthKit bodyMass
Health Connect WeightRecord
Manual entry
access: Withings free plan for up to 10 users (Withings+ needed for accounts created after 12 Oct 2026); HealthKit read or export; Health Connect READ_WEIGHT.
sampling: Semi-passive: each weigh-in uploads automatically; use a weekly mean of at least 3 morning weighings.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 2.35 kg (2.16 and 2.55 kg in two cohorts) for single fasted weighings two weeks apart, computed by us from an SD of change of 1.2 kg; recommend 2.4 kg.
mdc.population: 46 free-living adults, on average weight-stable (Bhutani 2017)

als_evidence: In 2,420 Dutch patients, 67.5% had lost weight by diagnosis (mean 5.5% in spinal and 6.9% in bulbar onset), including 35.1% without swallowing problems, and each extra 10% lost raised the risk of death by 23% (abstract only). Recalled weights show BMI falling in the years before diagnosis, but no study has tracked home-scale weights before diagnosis.
feeds_tool: HOME_TESTS weight (region general) with MDC 2.4 kg on weekly means; a confirmed loss prompts the clinician to ask and record weight_loss in a note (Mei weight 2.20). Today a weight-only decline also fires unclear_with_decline.
pitfalls: Christmas adds about 1.1 kg on average; weekday swing about 0.35%; time of day, clothing and hydration; a loss of about 0.64 kg a month (the median before the first visit in Shimizu 2012, at a height of 1.75 m) takes about 3.7 months to pass the MDC, so also test the slope and a 5% cumulative mark; a scale costs USD 129.95 or CAD 149.99.

devices_apis: Withings scales (measure types 5, 6, 8, 76 and segmental 173 to 175)
Galaxy Watch4 or later bioimpedance (Samsung Health Sensor SDK)
Fitbit Aria body fat (Google Health API)
access: As for weight; Galaxy Watch bioimpedance needs a Samsung partnership to distribute.
sampling: Each weigh-in on a scale, or a spot reading on a watch.

mdc.text: Least significant change about 1.9 kg of fat-free mass for smartwatch bioimpedance, computed by us from a precision RMSE of 0.7 kg.
mdc.population: 75 multiethnic adults (Bennett 2022, abstract only)

als_evidence: With research-grade bioimpedance, a low phase angle and falling fat-free mass predicted shorter survival in diagnosed ALS (abstract only). Consumer scales and watches are unvalidated in ALS; scales had fat-mass errors of several kilograms against DXA, and a watch's muscle estimate agreed weakly with DXA.
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: Proprietary equations built on healthy people; ALS muscle wasting and fluid shifts may bias them further; bias grows with body fat; weight stays the primary signal.

devices_apis: HealthKit restingHeartRate and heartRateVariabilitySDNN (RMSSD type from iOS 27)
Health Connect RestingHeartRateRecord and HeartRateVariabilityRmssdRecord
Google Health API daily-resting-heart-rate and daily-heart-rate-variability
Oura, WHOOP, Garmin and Withings APIs
access: Per-platform read permission.
sampling: Passive, daily or nightly.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 8.4 bpm for a single day's resting heart rate, computed by us from a within-person SD of 3.03 bpm.
mdc.population: 92,457 Fitbit users over a median 320 days (Quer 2020)

als_evidence: With a consumer chest strap, 68 people with diagnosed ALS had lower HRV and a higher heart rate than 56 healthy people, and in 102 newly diagnosed people HRV fell further over 12 months (both abstract only). No wrist or ring HRV study exists in ALS, and no study shows HRV change before diagnosis.
feeds_tool: Context only; after diagnosis a sustained rise in resting heart rate could prompt a check for infection or hypoventilation.
pitfalls: Not specific: age, fitness, anxiety, alcohol, infection and drugs move it; watch N-N interval error 31.31% at rest; Apple may replace same-day resting heart rate samples, so re-read recent days.

devices_apis: Apple Watch sleep stages (HealthKit sleep analysis)
Health Connect SleepSessionRecord
Google Health API sleep
Withings Sleep (wakeupcount, out_of_bed_count)
Oura, Samsung and Garmin
access: Per-platform read permission.
sampling: Passive, nightly.
als_evidence: By sleep lab or questionnaire, about half of people with diagnosed ALS have a sleep disorder, with shorter and more broken sleep (abstract only). Presymptomatic gene carriers show EEG sleep changes, but consumer trackers cannot measure these and no wearable sleep study exists in ALS.
feeds_tool: Context only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: Consumer deep-sleep ICC 0.13 to 0.36 against a sleep lab; devices sometimes record nothing; depression, night-time urination, cramps, pain and sleeping pills; NIV changes the signal.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 8 or later: HealthKit appleSleepingWristTemperature
Health Connect SkinTemperatureRecord
Google Health API skin temperature
Withings, Oura and WHOOP
access: Per-platform read permission; Apple's type is read-only.
sampling: Passive, one value per night.
als_evidence: No study has tested wrist or skin temperature as a sign of ALS in people; a review notes disturbed thermoregulation in ALS animal models and calls for human studies (abstract only). Closest use outside ALS: Apple lists exercise, jet lag, menstrual cycles and illness as causes of change.
feeds_tool: Context only, as a flag for possible fever and for cold nights when SpO2 may be unreliable.
pitfalls: Apple Watch wrist temperature is not yet validated, even in healthy people; illness, exercise, travel and menstrual cycles move it.

devices_apis: Phone microphone (Red-Flag Navigator reading test)
WatchALS iPhone app with AWS Transcribe (research)
ResearchKit audio tasks (iOS)
access: None; runs in the browser today.
sampling: Active, weekly, about 1 minute; same passage at the same time of day.

mdc.text: MDC95 22.1 wpm in ALS and 31.3 wpm in controls for weekly home iPhone readings of the Bamboo passage (WatchALS); the header says %MDC95 but the text gives wpm. Recommend 31 wpm before diagnosis and 22 after.
mdc.population: 19 people with ALS and 23 controls, weekly home tests over 24 weeks (WatchALS)

als_evidence: Speaking rate fell 1.74 wpm a month in spinal onset and 4.16 in bulbar onset in 166 diagnosed people, and people who rated their speech as only mildly affected (speech item 3) already read slower than controls (136 against 174 wpm remotely). On home phones, 11 people with normal bulbar scores spoke 0.77 SD slower than 21 controls.
feeds_tool: HOME_TESTS reading (region bulbar): weekly mean of same-day readings at the same time of day, MDC 31 wpm before diagnosis and 22 wpm after; a decline adds home_decline in bulbar.
pitfalls: Limb-onset change over 8 weeks is only about 0.3 to 3.2 wpm (computed by us); practice raises scores (0.25 wpm a week in controls); time of day matters (Alex: 165 against 118 wpm); reading ability, vision, accent, colds and room noise; our passage and button timing differ from WatchALS.

devices_apis: Phone microphone (same reading recording)
Modality.AI canonical timing alignment (CTA)
Aural Analytics articulatory precision (AP)
Apple SensorKit telephony and Siri speech metrics (research-only)
access: Percent pause and articulation rate need only an on-device pause detector; CTA and AP are proprietary; SensorKit is research-only.
sampling: Active, from the weekly reading or a fast pa-ta-ka task; passive only through SensorKit.

mdc.text: Articulatory precision MDC 0.85 on a 0 to 10 scale on home phones, measured over days 15 to 45; percent pause MDC95 9.39 points in lab and clinic controls (Barnett 2020).
mdc.population: All available participants from two home-phone studies of 110 people with ALS and 26 healthy people, days 15 to 45 (Stegmann 2024)

als_evidence: Percent pause separated people with ALS and normal bulbar scores from controls (AUC 0.83, against 0.65 for rate), and remote timing alignment reached its MCID in 3.86 weeks in bulbar and 8.32 weeks in non-bulbar onset. Articulatory precision and speaking rate caught bulbar change before the ALSFRS-R bulbar subscale did, all in diagnosed people.
feeds_tool: Context beside reading rate until its home noise is measured; later a second output of the bulbar test, with only one bulbar test allowed to escalate.
pitfalls: most authors of the Modality papers work for the company; AP compares speech with American English; cognitive impairment changes pauses; the lab MDC for percent pause may not match home noise.

devices_apis: Phone microphone
VOC-ALS dataset (Samsung Galaxy S8+, 8 kHz, one clinic session)
access: Research only; VOC-ALS needs a Synapse account and may not be redistributed.
sampling: Active sustained vowels and syllable repetition.

mdc.text: No phone MDC in ALS. Phone repeatability: median ICC 0.31 for sustained-vowel features, 0.55 for sentence reading and 0.02 for connected speech; only 11% of features above 0.75.
mdc.population: 72 people with ALS and 22 controls over the first 7 days in a mobile app, plus 24 people with ALS and suspected FTD tested weekly; medians pooled across the samples (Stegmann 2020 repeatability study)

als_evidence: In VOC-ALS (102 diagnosed ALS, 51 controls, one clinic session), 10 features differed across groups, mostly pitch variability and jitter, but non-dysarthric patients did not differ from controls on the strongest feature. A meta-analysis found jitter, shimmer and noise-to-harmonics ratio separated bulbar ALS from controls (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Research only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: Phone jitter and shimmer error is large and phone signal processing distorts voice-quality measures; sex and language affect features; VOC-ALS is Italian only.

devices_apis: Phone camera
access: Research method; nothing to install.
sampling: Active, a short video of side-to-side tongue movement.
als_evidence: In 37 people with ALS and 20 controls, side-to-side tongue movement frequency was 0.14 against 0.40, linked to dysarthria but not to swallowing trouble (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Research only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: One small cross-sectional study; no reliability data; lighting and camera angle uncontrolled at home.

devices_apis: EAT-10 questionnaire in the app
access: None.
sampling: Active, about 1 minute, weekly or monthly.
als_evidence: Against videofluoroscopy in 70 diagnosed people, an EAT-10 score of 3 or more detected penetration or aspiration (sensitivity 88%) and 8 or more detected aspiration (negative predictive value 95.5%), with similar results in two other cohorts. All were given in clinic, on paper where stated; app delivery and phone swallow sounds are unvalidated in ALS.
feeds_tool: Not a home-test decline: a score of 3 or more (or 8 or more) prompts the clinician to ask about and record dysphagia in a note (Mei weight 4.57) and to refer for a swallow assessment.
pitfalls: Self-report misses early change that patients do not notice; cognitive impairment; no test-retest data.

devices_apis: Phone microphone
access: Research method.
sampling: Active, a few voluntary coughs.
als_evidence: A phone app estimate of cough peak flow agreed with a flow meter (ICC 0.774) in 50 neuromuscular patients including 26 with ALS (abstract only). In 60 people with ALS and 40 controls, phone cough sounds separated ALS from controls (AUC 0.85) and were linked to the ALSFRS-R total, but not to measured cough peak flow.
feeds_tool: Research only, not fed to the engine.
pitfalls: The two studies conflict; clinic settings only; daily home cough-flow checks reached only 37% compliance.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 6 or later or Ultra: HealthKit oxygenSaturation (US LW/A and LS/A models computed on the iPhone)
Samsung Galaxy Watch (Health Connect OxygenSaturationRecord)
Fitbit and Pixel Watch (Google Health API oxygen-saturation)
Withings ScanWatch (spo2_auto)
Garmin Pulse Ox (Garmin API only)
access: Per-platform read permission; in Health Connect only Samsung wrote SpO2 among the brands checked; Withings may need its Advanced Biomarkers plan.
sampling: Passive overnight if the device is worn in bed; summarise 3-night blocks as T90 or ODI.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 9.5 events per hour for ODI and about 14.7 points for T90, computed by us from night-to-night ICCs of 0.901 and 0.940 and night-1 SDs of 10.9 events per hour and 21.7 points, with a clinic wrist oximeter; crude, because T90 is skewed.
mdc.population: 100 people with MND, 132 three-night studies, Nonin WristOx2 clinical wrist oximeter (Luu 2025)

als_evidence: With clinic oximeters in diagnosed ALS, overnight oximetry turned abnormal a median 1.6 years after onset against 3.8 years for FVC below 50% of predicted (476 people, abstract only), and mean night SpO2 below 93% went with shorter survival (69 people, abstract only). No consumer watch or ring SpO2 has been tested in ALS.
feeds_tool: Context only: a sustained 3-night pattern (T90 above about 5% to 10% or ODI above 15 per hour) prompts a clinic overnight oximetry, and after diagnosis an NIV review. Never lower a risk because SpO2 looks normal.
pitfalls: Over-reads in darker skin (occult low oxygen nearly 3 times as common in Black patients); accuracy worse below 88%; about 30% of wrist night data lost; misses about a third of hypoventilation; cold hands, tattoos and motion; the US Apple Watch redesign.

devices_apis: Apple Watch: HealthKit respiratoryRate
Fitbit and Pixel Watch: Google Health API daily-respiratory-rate
Health Connect RespiratoryRateRecord (written by the Google Health app)
Withings Sleep rr
Garmin respiration (Garmin API)
Oura and WHOOP (own APIs; respiratory rate not confirmed)
access: Per-platform read permission; in Health Connect only the Google Health app wrote it among the brands checked.
sampling: Passive, one value per night.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 2.1 breaths a minute (14-day CV 5%, near the average) to 3.9 (CV 9.2%, top of the young-women range) at 15.4 breaths a minute, computed by us.
mdc.population: Fitbit users aged 20 to 69, assumed healthy; mean 14-day CV about 4.7% to 7.4% by age and sex; 90% range 2.3% to 9.2% in women aged 20 to 24 and up to 21.7% in men aged 65 to 69 (Natarajan 2021)

als_evidence: No ALS study has used wearable breathing rate. Indirectly, neuromuscular patients without breathing complaints breathe fast and shallow (20 people including 2 with ALS, abstract only), and on home NIV breathing rate in ALS rose more when tidal volume was low.
feeds_tool: Context only: a rise of more than about 2 to 4 breaths a minute above the person's own baseline, lasting weeks, prompts a check.
pitfalls: Infection raises it (36.4% of COVID-symptomatic Fitbit users had a night at least 3 breaths a minute above usual); weight and age; accuracy falls in severe sleep apnea; Apple and Withings rates unvalidated; ventilator logs are better once NIV starts.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, SE 3: Breathing Disturbances and sleep apnea notifications (HealthKit)
Withings Sleep under-mattress pad: breathing_disturbances_intensity, AHI (EU and Australia), withings_index (US Sleep Rx)
access: HealthKit read permission; Withings user.sleepevents scope (Withings+ for new accounts); Withings lists the cleared AHI only on its paid Advanced Biomarkers plan.
sampling: Passive, nightly; Apple analyses 30-day windows and needs at least 10 nights.

mdc.text: No MDC. Against a home sleep test, Withings AHIs averaged over 1, 3 or 7 nights were not equivalent within 2.5 events per hour; this is accuracy, not night-to-night noise.
mdc.population: 35 patients with suspected sleep apnea tested against home sleep testing, Mayo Clinic (Jagielski 2022, abstract only)

als_evidence: In a sleep lab, 45.6% of 250 non-ventilated people with ALS had an AHI above 5 and 40% had hypoventilation, and in mild ALS a higher AHI predicted new breathlessness within 12 months (both abstract only). Consumer apnea features have not been tested in ALS, and in 43 people AHI did not correlate with vital capacity while minimum SpO2 did (abstract only).
feeds_tool: Context only: prompts a sleep study, and after diagnosis a question about breathlessness lying flat.
pitfalls: Apple's feature excludes people already diagnosed with sleep apnea and is not for managing it; devices learned obstructive apnea patterns, not REM hypoventilation; Withings' own study reported better accuracy than independent studies; AHI availability depends on region.

devices_apis: Home handheld spirometer (some with a phone connection)
access: Clinic-supplied device, ideally with one coached session; no consumer platform stores lung function.
sampling: Active, every 1 to 4 weeks.

mdc.text: No home test-retest MDC found. Unsupervised home vital capacity agreed with supervised tests within -15.1 to +15.4% of predicted at baseline.
mdc.population: 33 people with MND, unsupervised home tests every 4 weeks (Helleman 2022)

als_evidence: In 233 trial participants, coached home vital capacity matched clinic values (Lin's r 0.82) and fell 1.882% of predicted a month (abstract only), and in a remote study of 67 people, the FVC slopes of the 34 who could be grouped clustered into slow, moderate and fast groups. Breathing is the first symptom in only about 3% of people with ALS.
feeds_tool: A monitoring view after diagnosis, not the referral engine; NICE-based guidance says to discuss NIV at a vital capacity below 50%, or below 80% with symptoms.
pitfalls: Effort-dependent; weak lips and face make it harder; 15% felt they did worse than in clinic; slopes need about 3 months to settle.

devices_apis: Phone microphone: speech-based FVC model (Aural Analytics)
Phone microphone: maximum phonation time
Phone microphone: percent pause in reading
access: Maximum phonation time and percent pause are simple to build; the FVC model is proprietary.
sampling: Active, a sustained vowel or the weekly reading.

mdc.text: No MDC. The speech FVC model had repeatability ICC 0.92 to 0.94 (spirometry 0.97) and a mean absolute error of 0.54 to 0.58 L (18.5% to 19.5%).
mdc.population: People with ALS using a phone app (Stegmann 2021, abstract only)

als_evidence: Speech-estimated FVC correlated 0.80 with measured FVC and picked up decline, though less than spirometry (abstract only). In 62 diagnosed people, maximum phonation time predicted impaired cough peak flow (AUC 0.88), and percent pause in a home phone reading flagged vital capacity below 50% with AUC 0.88 in 36 people.
feeds_tool: Context only, as a soft trend between spirometry tests.
pitfalls: An error of about 19% is too coarse for NIV decisions; no phone test-retest data for maximum phonation time; bulbar weakness affects voice tasks.

devices_apis: Phone microphone in the browser (Red-Flag Navigator pa-ta-ka test, app/js/home/audio.js)
WatchALS iPhone app (research)
access: None; the browser timing tool is built but not validated. Needs HTTPS and microphone permission.
sampling: Active, weekly, under a minute; WatchALS used 15 s of fast 'pa-ta-ka' on an iPhone.

mdc.text: MDC 1.03 syllables per second in ALS and 1.05 in controls from weekly home iPhone tests (the table header says %MDC95, but the units are syllables per second).
mdc.population: 19 people with ALS (15 limb onset) and 23 controls, weekly home iPhone tests over 24 weeks (WatchALS)

als_evidence: In WatchALS (19 diagnosed ALS, 23 controls, iPhone) the weekly pa-ta-ka rate had test-retest ICC 0.91 in ALS, but the baseline rate did not differ significantly from controls. Early change is mixed: one small study found a slower /ta/ before bulbar symptoms (4.80 against 5.51 syllables per second), and two other cohorts found no difference.
feeds_tool: Kit test ddk_rate (region bulbar), weekly after 2 practice sessions. Before diagnosis only a second output of the bulbar test, never a separate escalator; after diagnosis, monitoring.
pitfalls: Scores rise with practice, so do 2 practice sessions before the baseline. Automatic counters struggle with severe dysarthria and with /ta/: the best energy-envelope counter had limits of agreement of -5.92 to +7.12 syllables against manual counts in 145 people with ALS. One of the two null cohorts (Kadambi 2023) could be re-checked only at abstract level. Our browser counter is a timing tool, not validated.

devices_apis: Phone microphone in the browser (Red-Flag Navigator long 'aah' test, app/js/home/audio.js)
Remote speech platform (Modality, research)
access: None; the browser timing tool is built but not validated.
sampling: Active, a few minutes, after diagnosis; several tries per session (Moreno 2021 took the best of 3).

mdc.text: MDD 5.54 to 8.55 s in healthy adults retested 15 days apart (best of 3 tries). In ALS on a remote speech platform the test-retest ICC was 0.94 (sustained /i/), with no MDC given.
mdc.population: 90 healthy adults retested 15 days apart (Moreno 2021)

als_evidence: In 62 diagnosed people tested every 3 months, an MPT of 10 s or less flagged a peak cough flow of 160 L/min or less with sensitivity 0.88 and specificity 0.82 (one row of the published accuracy table, chosen by us). On a remote speech platform in 54 people with ALS the test-retest ICC was 0.94, and MPT change tracked slow vital capacity change (r = 0.67).
feeds_tool: Kit test mpt (region breathing). After diagnosis a short MPT prompts a real cough-flow or vital-capacity test; it never feeds the referral engine.
pitfalls: Depends on effort, instructions and speech, so it is not a pure breathing measure. Later tries tend to be longer (Shinoda 2016), and in 380 older adults trial-to-trial limits ran from -5.0 to +7.7 s. This adds to the 'Phone lung-function estimate' entry, which says no phone test-retest data exist for MPT: Neumann 2026 reports test-retest data in ALS from a remote speech platform (device not stated).

devices_apis: Phone microphone in the browser (Red-Flag Navigator counting test, app/js/home/audio.js)
Counting aloud to a nurse by phone (no device)
access: None; the browser timing tool is built but not validated, and the count can also be done by phone with no device.
sampling: Active, under a minute: one full breath, then count aloud in a normal voice (Ali 2010 paced it with a metronome at 2 counts per second; Moreno 2021 let people self-pace).

mdc.text: MDD 11 to 18 counts in healthy adults retested 15 days apart (self-paced, usual pitch and loudness).
mdc.population: Healthy adults retested 15 days apart (Moreno 2021)

als_evidence: In 30 people with ALS the count flagged FVC under 50% with sensitivity 100% and specificity 56% to 60% (AUC 0.696). In 100 people with neuromuscular disorders (the number with ALS is not stated), an upright count under 39 flagged an NIV indication (sensitivity 0.92, specificity 0.46) and under 41 flagged FVC under 80% (0.89, 0.62).
feeds_tool: Kit test single_breath_count (region breathing). After diagnosis a low or falling count prompts a real vital-capacity test; it never feeds the referral engine.
pitfalls: Depends on effort, pace, posture and speech; keep the same posture and pace every week. Both accuracy studies (Quinn 2021 in ALS, Klein 2023 in neuromuscular disorders) were read as abstracts only, and in Quinn 2021 accuracy was higher in people with little speech involvement.

devices_apis: Stopwatch or phone timer (Red-Flag Navigator stopwatch test)
A sturdy armchair against a wall and a mark 3 m away
access: None; a helper starts and stops the timer and stays close.
sampling: Active, weekly or every 2 weeks, about 1 minute; usual pace with the usual walking aid.

mdc.text: MDC95 3.0 s in older adults at high fall risk retested 1 week apart; 1.4 s in 52 older adults; MDD95 22.6% for a fast TUG done remotely in myotonic dystrophy type 1.
mdc.population: 30 older adults at high fall risk, retested 1 week apart (Intaruk 2024)

als_evidence: In 31 people with ALS tested monthly, TUG rose steadily, and 14 s went with a 10% chance of falling over 6 months, which the authors proposed as a prompt for mobility aids (abstract only). In 224 people followed for 12 months, 57.6% fell and each extra second of TUG raised the odds of falling by 8.3%.
feeds_tool: Kit test tug_time (region leg): monitoring and fall risk, not an escalator (the timed walk speed is the leg escalator). A TUG of 14 s or more prompts a mobility-aid and falls review.
pitfalls: No ALS test-retest MDC; the published MDCs come from supervised older adults, and unsupervised home noise is probably larger. Do it only with someone in the room after any fall or near-fall in the last 3 months, with a walking aid, or once the TUG is 14 s or more (our rule). Restart the baseline when shoes, brace or aid change.

devices_apis: Stopwatch or phone timer (Red-Flag Navigator stopwatch test)
A sturdy chair with arms, against a wall
access: None.
sampling: Active, weekly or every 2 weeks: stands in 30 seconds with arms folded, or the time for five full stands.

mdc.text: Five-times sit-to-stand MDC95 3.5 s (older adults at high fall risk, 1 week) and 1.6 s (52 older adults); 30-second chair stand MDC95 4.25 stands (150 post-COVID adults, about 2 weeks).
mdc.population: 30 older adults at high fall risk retested 1 week apart (Intaruk 2024); 150 post-COVID adults for the 30-second test (Braun 2026)

als_evidence: Only pilots in ALS: in 8 people, TUG and five-times sit-to-stand raised heart rate without acute changes in heart-rate variability, and a 7-person home resistance-training pilot used sit-to-stand as an outcome. The 30-second chair stand has not been studied in ALS, though in 28 people with spinal stenosis a video-call version agreed with in-person testing (ICC 0.83 to 0.88 across three tests).
feeds_tool: Kit tests sts30 and sts5_time (region leg): context and monitoring only.
pitfalls: Skip it once the person needs their arms to rise or cannot stand without help, and do it only with someone in the room after a fall or near-fall (our rules). No ALS MDC; the published ones come from supervised sessions.

devices_apis: ALSFRS-R-SE (self-explanatory version, listed by Mapi as public domain under CC BY 4.0), on paper or in an app
ALSFRS-R self-entry online or in an app (licence from Mapi Research Trust)
access: The ALSFRS-R is copyrighted (Cedarbaum 1999, distributed by Mapi Research Trust) and every electronic version needs a licence for every user, with fees for commercial and funded users. The ALSFRS-R-SE is listed by Mapi as public domain under CC BY 4.0.
sampling: Active, monthly after diagnosis, a few minutes; read by domain.

mdc.text: Repeat self-entry limits of agreement 4.3 points on the total and 1.6 to 2.4 points by domain.
mdc.population: 59 people with MND (Bakker 2020)

als_evidence: Self-entered scores agree well with clinician ratings: ICC 0.93 in 60 people, r 0.96 online against clinic in 127, and ICC 0.925 to 0.961 with weekly app entry in 19, where self-scores ran 1.3 points higher. Its repeat noise (4.3 points) is larger than the 0.9 to 2.0 points it falls in 8 weeks (computed by us), so it suits monthly monitoring, not an 8-week referral trigger.
feeds_tool: Not a kit test tonight. Monthly monitoring after diagnosis, by domain; never fires unclear_with_decline.
pitfalls: Self-administered versions differ from one another (Allen 2025), and whether the ALSFRS-R-SE may be adapted is an open question. The stair item had among the lowest self-versus-interview agreement (60.6% to 70.8%).

devices_apis: Validated upper-arm cuff (Hypertension Canada recommended devices)
HealthKit bloodPressure correlation (systolic plus diastolic)
Health Connect BloodPressureRecord (READ_BLOOD_PRESSURE)
Bluetooth Blood Pressure service, for cuffs that use it (app/js/home/import/bluetooth.js)
access: HealthKit read or the Health export; Health Connect permission; Web Bluetooth in Chrome and Edge (not on iOS, in Safari or in Firefox); typed-in readings.
sampling: Active: the home protocol is 2 morning and 2 evening readings for 7 days; after diagnosis, a lying-then-standing reading when asked.

mdc.text: MDC95 about 13.5/9.2 mmHg for a 2-day home mean and about 7.2/4.9 mmHg for 7 independent days, computed by us as 1.96 times SDs of differences of 6.9/4.7 mmHg.
mdc.population: 133 untreated adults; home readings on 6 workdays within 2 weeks, compared as 2-day means (Stergiou 2002)

als_evidence: Blood pressure does not flag ALS, and as an early sign the evidence goes against it (the notes grade that contradicted): hypertension more than a year before diagnosis was not linked to motor neuron disease in 1,463 Swedish patients, and in 3,714 US Medicare patients it was slightly less common 2 years or more before diagnosis (OR 0.91). The moderate grade is only for the lying-to-standing test after diagnosis, which found orthostatic hypotension in 11.1% to 13.1% of 1,240 trial patients, though only 22.5% of them still had it at follow-up.
feeds_tool: Signal bp, context only (Route 3): shown beside the score, never a motor-region decline. After diagnosis, dizziness on standing or drugs linked to orthostatic hypotension prompt a lying-then-standing reading; a fall of more than 20 systolic or 10 diastolic mmHg within 3 minutes of standing prompts a medication and fluid review (Route 2).
pitfalls: The grade is the standing test's (moderate). As an early sign of ALS the evidence goes against blood pressure; the notes grade that 'contradicted', which this schema has no value for. A CMAJ patient guide says more than 85% of home monitors sold worldwide are not accurate, so use a Hypertension Canada device, and repeat a standing test before acting.

devices_apis: Apple Watch Series 9 or later, or Ultra 2 or later, with iPhone 11 or later
HealthKit hypertensionEvent (iOS 26.2 and later, no description in the docs)
access: Adults 22 or older who were never diagnosed with hypertension and are not pregnant; HealthKit read of the event type.
sampling: Passive; the iPhone pools the watch's optical scores over 30-day periods.

mdc.text: No MDC: a yes-or-no alert. About 7.7% false alerts per 30 days, computed by us from the specificity of 92.3%.
mdc.population: 1,863 adults never diagnosed with hypertension who wore the watch 15 days or more (FDA K250507)

als_evidence: No ALS study exists. In the FDA submission the alert had sensitivity 41.2% and specificity 92.3% in people never diagnosed with hypertension, and it is not meant for anyone already diagnosed.
feeds_tool: Not used.
pitfalls: Misses about 59% of people with hypertension (computed by us). After an alert Apple asks for a 7-day cuff log, which is the reading worth having.

devices_apis: Samsung Galaxy Watch blood pressure (Samsung Health Monitor; upper-arm cuff calibration every 28 days)
Hilo (formerly Aktiia) bracelet, cuff-calibrated
Biobeat cuffless monitor (FDA K241066)
access: Samsung needs a Galaxy phone with Android 12 or later; it holds a Health Canada Class II licence and no FDA clearance was found. Aktiia G0 is cleared in the US only for ages 22 to 59, recalibrated every 24 h.
sampling: Passive or spot checks between cuff calibrations.

mdc.text: No MDC. Watch error grew to 3.4/5.1 mmHg when blood pressure was 10 mmHg from the calibration value; a bracelet had an SD of differences of about 10 mmHg systolic in people aged 65 to 85.
mdc.population: Galaxy Watch5 against an upper-arm cuff in 37 people over 28 days (Walzel 2026); 35 people aged 65 to 85 without diabetes (Theiler 2023)

als_evidence: No ALS study exists. These devices lose accuracy when blood pressure moves away from the calibration value, which is exactly what an orthostatic drop or an autonomic swing is, and Samsung Canada says not to use its feature with a neurological disorder such as tremor.
feeds_tool: Not used; a validated upper-arm cuff is the only blood pressure device worth recommending.
pitfalls: European Society of Hypertension statements say guidelines do not recommend cuffless devices, and a 2026 statement says they are not for clinical decisions.

devices_apis: Apple Watch ECG (HealthKit HKElectrocardiogram, read-only, a lead similar to lead I)
KardiaMobile 6L (AliveCor)
Samsung ECG app
Withings ECG app
Fitbit and Pixel Watch ECG (Google Health API electrocardiogram type)
access: HealthKit read (Apple Watch only) or the ECG CSVs in the Apple Health export; the Google Health API electrocardiogram type; Health Connect has no ECG type.
sampling: Active 30-s recording when asked.

mdc.text: No test-retest data. QTc from a 6-lead home device differed from a 12-lead ECG by a mean absolute 12 ± 9 ms, and 7% of tracings were unreadable.
mdc.population: 234 outpatients, mean age 57, 57% with heart disease (Bergeman 2023)

als_evidence: Average QTc is normal in diagnosed ALS; in 12 patients QTc and its dispersion rose from the early to the terminal stage, and Holter ECGs were normal in all 35 patients of a cardiac MRI study despite MRI changes (abstracts only). Atrial fibrillation was slightly less common 24 months or more before diagnosis (OR 0.81), so rhythm checks do not flag ALS.
feeds_tool: Not a home test. After diagnosis, a clinician-read QTc check at baseline and 3 to 4 hours after the first dose of dextromethorphan/quinidine in people at risk of QT prolongation (US label).
pitfalls: Watch rhythm features classify AFib and sinus rhythm; they do not report QTc, so a clinician reads the tracing. Unreadable tracings happen (7% in Bergeman 2023).

devices_apis: 64-electrode high-density surface EMG grid with SPiQE software (clinic research)
Home high-density surface EMG in trials (RHAALS, SEPALS-2; no results yet)
Consumer EMG wearables (Meta Neural Band exposes gestures, not raw EMG)
access: Research only; no consumer device gives raw EMG twitch counts.
sampling: Active: a 15- to 30-minute resting recording per muscle.

mdc.text: No MDC. Same-day ICC 0.95 in the biceps and 0.44 to 0.62 in the calf; 15-minute recordings agreed with 30-minute ones with ICC 0.78 to 0.98.
mdc.population: 10 people with ALS recorded 3 times in a day (biceps n = 19, calf n = 20) (Bashford 2020); 20 ALS and 5 benign fasciculation syndrome for recording length (Crook-Rumsey 2022)

als_evidence: In the clinic, a 30-minute biceps recording separated 39 people with ALS from 25 controls (AUC 0.89; above 13.7 twitches a minute, sensitivity 79.5% and specificity 96%). Home recordings are in trials with no results yet, and twitch rates fall as a muscle weakens, so a count cannot use the worse-than-baseline rule.
feeds_tool: Not used. Ask about twitching instead and prompt the GP to examine; only a GP-recorded fasciculation carries the Mei weight (adjusted OR 40.2) (Route 2).
pitfalls: Healthy people twitch: surface electrodes found twitches in 77% of 122 healthy adults, and benign twitching persisted for 8 months to several years in 98.3% of 180 people, none of whom developed motor neuron dysfunction. People with ALS noticed twitches in only 0.28 muscle groups on average (19 people).

devices_apis: Skulpt Scanner (consumer electrical impedance myography; discontinued)
Myolex mScan (IRB-approved research only)
access: Not available: Skulpt stopped selling its scanner, the Myolex mScan is for IRB-approved research only, and no FDA clearance was found.
sampling: Active; ALS At Home measured daily for 90 days, then twice weekly to 9 months (biceps, forearms, calves and quadriceps).

mdc.text: No home MDC. In clinic, same-session ICC 0.95 with one evaluator (0.91 to 0.98 across muscles) and 0.91 with two (0.78 to 0.96).
mdc.population: 46 people with ALS, 30 with mimics and 30 healthy people at 6 sites (Shefner 2018)

als_evidence: Daily home readings of the left biceps cut the estimated trial size to 46 per arm against 710 with monthly readings, though a published letter disputes the size of that gain. EIM did not separate ALS from mimics (AUC 0.60), so it monitors but does not detect.
feeds_tool: Not used: no device can be bought.
pitfalls: The lead investigator holds equity in Myolex, and a Myolex employee co-authored Shefner 2018. Some ALS At Home participants feared watching their values fall.

devices_apis: Phone or laptop camera with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (21 hand landmarks, runs in the browser)
access: Buildable in the browser over HTTPS with camera permission; not built.
sampling: Active, under a minute per hand.
als_evidence: No ALS study of hand video was found; the only related hit was in children with SMA using a depth camera. In Parkinson's disease a webcam screen reached AUROC 0.85 to 0.87 and agreed with specialists with kappa 0.59.
feeds_tool: Not used; phone touchscreen tapping covers the hand tonight.
pitfalls: In a 10-person lab check, the 2D error rose with tapping speed and depth removed most of it (Amprimo 2023, a preprint). The one home test-retest figure in the notes (ICC 0.65) could not be re-checked, so none is given here.

devices_apis: ECAS by video call (clinician-administered)
ALS-CBS by telephone (clinician-administered)
Online carer behaviour questionnaires
access: Clinician-run. The ECAS form is copyrighted by the University of Edinburgh (all rights reserved) and app licensing is not confirmed.
sampling: Active, at diagnosis and when there is concern; the ECAS takes 15 to 20 minutes.

mdc.text: Reliable change 9 points on the ECAS total with alternate forms over 4 months (8 for the ALS-specific part, 4 for the rest), with no practice effect.
mdc.population: 57 healthy adults retested about 4 months apart with alternate forms (Crockford 2017)

als_evidence: About half of people with ALS have some cognitive or behavioural change, and 12.6% to 13.8% have frontotemporal dementia in two population studies. The ECAS by video call was equivalent to in-person testing in 27 people without ALS and had inter-rater ICC 0.99 in 24 with ALS, while the phone ALS-CBS agreed only moderately with in-person testing (ICC 0.50).
feeds_tool: Not a motor signal and not a kit test. After diagnosis a clinician screen (ECAS); before diagnosis a family's concern is a clinician prompt only. No engine_region: the engine's region would be cognitive, which this schema's list does not include.
pitfalls: The ECAS fluency index subtracts the person's own reading or copying time, so slow speech or hands do not count as slow thinking; a home fluency test scored by speech recognition has no ALS MDC, and the browser Web Speech API sends audio to a server by default. In independent samples, remote ECAS totals ran 6.2 points higher than face-to-face ones (Didcote 2024), so keep the same mode each time.
